findings.claim: Under the offline lock, the wrappers turn tracing off only with langsmith.tracing_context(enabled=False) and by stripping LangChainTracer from the run's own and inherited callbacks. langchain_core decides tracing by _tracing_v2_is_enabled(), which returns True first when tracing_v2_callback_var is set (langchain_core/tracers/context.py:141-144), before consulting ls_utils.tracing_is_enabled(); CallbackManager configure then adds that tracer_v2 to the run's manager (langchain_core/callbacks/manager.py:2483-2515), after the explicit callbacks were filtered. Nothing in src/ resets tracing_v2_callback_var, so a run under the lock started inside the caller's tracing_v2_enabled() context is traced to LangSmith, sending the run's inputs and statement data off the machine. This fails R29's 'LangSmith's own tracing is off whatever the environment says' and P18.
findings.repro: firm.yaml 'offline_lock: true'; monkeypatch LangChainTracer._persist_run/_start_trace to record runs (as the existing tests do); `from langchain_core.tracers.context import tracing_v2_enabled; with tracing_v2_enabled(client=types.SimpleNamespace()): build(llm.FakeLLM()).invoke({'statement_path': p}, {'configurable': {'thread_id': 't'}})`. The recorder sees the graph's runs (load, draft, ...). Fix: under the lock also set tracing_v2_callback_var to None for the run (and reset it after), alongside tracing_context(enabled=False).
